## Finding

Yes, a lot depends on the showcase. Every consumer lives inside the veneer repository or in scaffold's `.orkestrel/veneer` records. Nothing in another repository loads the page: the one "veneer" test in the browser repository uses inline markup (/home/user/browser/tests/src/browser/elements/BrowserDOMElementManager.test.ts:15-25).

Five test suites mount the page and drive it by role, accessible name, id, and class: the journey suite, three `app:browser` suites, and the `setup:browser` suite. The guide's § Showcase and the stage B plan also rely on it. Stage B uses the showcase journeys as its regression check.

A visual redesign can change colors, spacing, and the look of the chrome freely. It must keep these contracts, or change them together with the named tests:

- all 72 sections render in one document;
- the five-button header and its Tab order;
- a Contents region whose links render and are reachable at 390 px and 1280 px;
- the `.sticky-lg-top` inline-style contract;
- class tokens taken only from the registry;
- the width of the main column.

The mobile contents the user wants to fold breaks J1, J2, J3, four table arrangers, the contrast subjects, and the contents-offset case unless those change in the same unit.

## What a redesign can change, and what it must keep

A redesign can change these freely:

- **Chrome tone**: colors, shadows, radii, and type, through registry classes. The limits are 4.5:1 contrast on the header buttons and the four subjects, and a neutral header under the three faces.
- **Body layout classes**: the body container's padding, the row gutter, the heading sizes, and the contents link styling, apart from the uppercase text the group labels render.
- **Capture appearance**, because no test compares pixels.

Any change to the exact classes of the header, the bar, the controls, the brand, or the two nav wrappers fails factories.test.ts:805-867.

A redesign must keep these, or change them together with the named tests:

1. **All 72 sections stay in one document, rendered at once.** Each is a region named by an `h3` that matches its `SECTIONS` title, with the `SECTIONS` id. Each sits in `main > div` after an `h2#group-ID`. Readers: J3, `collectBootstrapGroups`, every component table, the census, partition, preservation, containment, and frozen-state cases.
   - Showing one section at a time breaks the whole journey suite.
   - "Isolated" can mean a distinct frame per section within the one page.
2. **Exactly five `header button` elements** with their labels, `value` attributes, `aria-pressed`, the two group names, and the status sentence. A sixth header button would also be toggled by `Showcase.ts:229-235`. The header stays sticky at top 0 with `z-index` 3, at or under 30% of the viewport height, each group's buttons on one row, and the brand left of the groups from 768 px.
3. **The Tab order**: skip link, the five buttons, then the Contents link `Containers`. Readers: J2 :386-401, the refusal walk :821, and setupBrowser.test.ts:3388.
4. **The Contents region at 390 and 1280**:
   - It is rendered, with exactly one rendered `nav`, and its visible text includes the uppercase group labels.
   - Every link renders and is reachable.
   - Readers: J1, J3, Showcase.test.ts:701-775, the arrangers at :4110, :4489, :4509, and :5796, and `collectContrastSubjects` in all four variants and at the default viewport.
   - A mobile contents that starts folded needs every one of these changed together, plus a capture state for the open drawer.
5. **`.sticky-lg-top` stays the only element with inline style at rest**, carrying only `top` and `max-height`, as written by `#offset`. Readers: integration.test.ts:1210-1222 and Showcase.test.ts:708-745.
6. **Class tokens come only from the registry**, plus `slide`, the icon tokens, and `TAILWIND_CLASSES`. No `style` attribute, no `inert`, unique ids, and every reference resolves. A new icon must also go into `ICONS` and templates.test.ts.
7. **No chrome class whose Tailwind rule departs.**
   - `collapse` reads `visibility: collapse` under `Tailwind, no layer` (setupBrowser.ts:814-818), so a `.collapse` sidebar vanishes under that face.
   - `container` reads 1280px against 1140px.
   - The partition case reads every chrome element that carries a shared name.
8. **The main column's width at 1280 and 390.**
   - The matrix hints hide from `xl`, so no matrix may scroll at 1280 (factories.ts:601).
   - Containment holds at both widths, and the chips stay legible at 390.
   - The scrollspy rows at 1280 and 390 depend on the width of the `ratio-4x3` Live examples frame (/home/user/veneer/app/browser/sections/live-components.html:7; setupBrowser.ts:5860-5918).
   - The navbar and responsive-offcanvas tables depend only on viewport breakpoints.
9. **The chrome needs no engine.** J2, J6, J7, and the header tables mount without one, so a toggle driven by the data API does nothing there. A chrome drawer must not reuse the dialog name `Sections` or the `Open the … drawer` names. It must not render a `role="dialog"` element on arrival, because J8 reads `countDialogs()` as 0.
10. **The section titles, `TAILWIND_READINGS` captions, and specimen names** the tests cite stay as they are, together with the guide's case citations, the 16 icon names, and the exact `@app/browser` export list.

No `.gitignore` entry, policy, or test forbids committing them. The page can reach `origin/main` with the fast-forward the campaign already uses, but GitHub can't display it for the user: the repository is private and Pages is off. So the user needs either the file opened locally after a pull, or a copy of the same bytes handed over in a viewable form.

## Where the page lives and how it builds

- **Scripts:** `build:showcase` and `build:showcase:vue` are at package.json:124-125, and the dev servers at :123 and :128. `prepublishOnly` (:127) builds both pages after `npm run build`.
- **Config:** configs/app/vite.showcase.config.ts:4 hands off to the `appShowcase` factory at vite.config.ts:364-394. That factory:
